slides.text:
`break` and `continue` only act on the innermost loop. A label gives a loop a name, so a statement deep inside can leave or skip a loop further out.

You will label `for`, `while` and `loop`, break out of nested loops, return a value from one, and label a plain block.

In nested loops, `break` leaves only the loop it sits in. The outer loop keeps going.

A label is a name that starts with a single quote, written before the loop. `break` and `continue` can then point at it.

Pseudo code, not Rust.
slides.code:
outer: repeat for each row
    repeat for each col
        if match found
            stop outer
        if col is not wanted
            skip to next outer

slides.text:
Any loop can carry a label: `for`, `while` and `loop`.

A labeled `loop` can also hand back a value: `break 'name value` ends that loop and the value becomes the result of the whole loop.

Even a plain block can have a label, and `break` leaves it early.

exercises.guide: Label a `while` loop and break out of it from an inner `for`.

Label the `while` loop. Each pass counts one try.

notes.text: The label goes before while, just like before for.
